citation: Khavari et al. (2023). A geospatial approach to understanding clean cooking challenges in sub-Saharan Africa. Nature Sustainability. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41893-022-01039-8
description: OnStove compares clean-cooking technology choices across raster cells in a user-defined study area. KTH and partners publish a Python package, documentation and case-study links. Inputs describe the available stoves, fuel and equipment costs, operating assumptions, population and spatial layers. The model calculates avoided morbidity, mortality, emissions and time use against capital, fuel and maintenance costs, then selects the option with the largest estimated net benefit in each cell. Geography and grid size are set by the supplied area and raster data. MIT-licensed code is public through GitHub and conda. A limitation is that the README describes an overnight technology switch; its calculated gains are an upper bound, not a forecast of adoption over time. OnStove supports household-energy access and fuel-supply planning. The catalogue's model-pypsa is a separate energy-system optimiser, not an OnStove component. A rejected round-one candidate concerns a Nepal result dataset, not this general model. No raster or case data were downloaded.
name: OnStove clean-cooking geospatial model
